title: Magic Online Theme Decks: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: Beauty stirs the memory like a sweet perfume excites the air.
The land drank power from the Mirari as though it had thirsted forever.
Olka collected the evening mist for years, studying its secrets. Once she learned its essence, she could vanish with a thought.
"All matter, animate or not, rots when exposed to time. We merely speed up the process." —Ezoc, Golgari rot farmer
One splash of the spring's water knocks you clear into last week.
Like his mother before him, Darigaaz gave his life defending Dominaria from the tyranny of self-styled "gods."
A regular guest at the Royal Masquerade, Arien is the envy of the Court. She appears in a new costume every hour.
The maze-like design embodies the core of Azorius law—strict structure designed to test wills and stall change.
Depending on your point of view, the seal represents a proud guardian of the natural cycle or one who has sold her soul to darkness for eternal life.
Gruul territorial markings need not be legible. The blood, snot, and muck used to smear them are unmistakably Gruul.
Made of bone and boiled in blood, a Rakdos signet is not considered finished until it has been used as a murder weapon.
Elves believe the hydra-god Progenitus sleeps beneath Naya, feeding on forgotten magics.
The symbol of the Conclave is one of unity, with tree supporting sun and sun feeding tree.

For the Simic Combine, its sigil serves not as an emblem of honor but as a trademark. Its familiar image on any biological commodity attests to superb craftsmanship, ingenious innovation, and higher cost.
A circle of sugar and a word of forbiddance.
The mind is a beautiful bounty encased in an annoying bone container.
Bant's hearts are as pure as its air and as bright as its skies.
The Capashen built the highest towers in Benalia to afford themselves the best view.
Llanowar has seven elfhames, or kingdoms, each with its own ruler. Their palaces are objects of awe, wonder, and envy.
Where wasted life cries out to be reborn.
Clear out the cell. Bring in the next prisoner.
The sky is the dragon's throne, the seat from which it issues its fiery decrees.
Jund is a world as cruel as those who call it home. Their brutal struggles scar the land even as it carves them in its image, a vicious circle spiraling out of control.
For wisdom's sake, it was built high to gaze on all things. For glory's sake, it was built high as a testament of power. For strength's sake, it was built high to repel all attacks.
"I am the purifier, the light that clears all shadows." —Seal inscription
"The so-called barbarians will not respect us for our military might—they will respect us for our honor." —Lucilde Fiksdotter, leader of the Order of the White Shield
"Four parts molten bronze, yes ... one part frozen mercury, yes, yes ... but then what?"
"No doubt the arbiters would put you away, after all the documents are signed. But I will have justice now." —Alovnek, Boros guildmage
"I don't understand why he works so hard on a device to duplicate a sound so easily made with hand and armpit." —Barrin, progress report
Simic mages create redundant backups of their experiments to reduce the consequences of catastrophe.
"Do not react to force in kind. Turn it aside. Direct it to where it can do no harm." —Meloku the Clouded Mirror
Unable to touch items of value, he goes forth to steal secrets instead.
"Beauty to the eye does not always translate to the touch." —Naimah, Femeref philosopher
In the depths of Rootwater, salvage and sewage differ only in texture.
"My brain hurts."
Friends teach what you want to know. Enemies teach what you *need* to know.
"There are two ways for me to pass this gate. One involves you remaining conscious." —Gerrard of the *Weatherlight*
"All rivers eventually run to the sea. My job is to sort out who goes first." —Maeveen O'Donagh, *Memoirs of a Soldier*
"Is it worse to walk while dead, or to be buried alive? I have witnessed both." —Crovax
Stinking of rot, it leaps between gravestones in search of its next meal.
Those who forget the horrors of the past are doomed to re-meet them.
An audience of one with the malice of thousands.
"An angel appeared in the smoldering skies above the fray, her clothes as flames, her armor as fire." —"Hymn of Angelfire"
"I'll take that. You won't need it when the revolution comes."
The time rifts remind Yavimaya of the enemies of its past and provide fresh fuel for its fires.
"For its time as a mortal, Anger chose a shell of boiling rock." —Scroll of Beginnings
"For dim-witted, thick-skulled genetic mutants, they have pretty good aim." —Sisay
Viashino thrashes keep iguanars as hunting companions, giving them wounded captives as playthings.
Keldons divide all their spoils into two groups: trophies and catapult ammunition.
"I do not teach. I simply reveal." —Daudi, Femeref tutor
"Only fools and bandits use roads."
"'I have arrived,' bellowed Brawn, and the plane shuddered." —Scroll of Beginnings
"These alleys are not safe. Come, I can guide you back to the market square."
"At harvest are seeds of next year sown."
"The elves can hide better than most can look." —Mwani, Mtenda herder
Before any major undertaking, a Cylian elf seeks the guidance of a visionary to learn the will of the gargantuan ancients.
She remembers every word spoken, from the hero's oath to the baby's cry.
Torching Krosa would be pointless. It grows faster than it burns.
The forest was too lush for the brothers to despoil—almost.
"First through the Riftstone was Genesis—and the world was lifeless no more." —Scroll of Beginnings
"Life's greatest lessons don't come from focus or concentration. They come from breathing and simply noticing." —Seton, centaur druid
The lion's only loyalty is to its hunger.
"The land grows only where the kami will it." —Dosan the Falling Leaf
Destroyed in one of the first battles of the Kami War, the town of Reito still grieved.
This cat has two lives and it's hunting for more.
Rath forces plants from its surface as one presses whey from cheese.
"The bones of the past will tell their tales—if you know how to speak their language." —Savra
As Gerrard made his escape, the wurm covered his flight by helping itself to three great mouthfuls of merfolk.
There were no tombstones in orochi territory. Slain warriors were buried with a tree sapling, so they would become a part of the forest after death.
He exercises his right to bear arms.
"Living scarecrows make a mockery of the natural order. Dead ones make fine hats."
It teaches *you* to play dead.
"Duty and law are the foundation on which civilization stands. They must not fall, for when they do, they take everything with them." —Lord Konda
Tall as a tree and probably related.
Secure in the embrace of wood, they want no part of Eladamri's war.
From each seed, a world. From each world, a thousand seeds.
"Don't laugh. It works." —Yavimaya ranger
Snaking remnants of nature directed by a body of thought and progress, the oracles embody all that is Simic.
A massive pull of mana caused all of Dominaria to pause—Multani had transplanted Yavimaya to Urborg's edge.
Not all silences are easily broken.
"Take a quiet moment to reflect on your sins." —Cleph, Order of Redeemed Souls
The smallest seed of regret can bloom into redemption.
Embermages aren't well known for their diplomatic skills.
Many ogres extracted blood oaths from the oni they summoned. Others simply extracted blood.
"I've been all over this world. I even remember some of those places."
"My destiny is to save others so their destinies may be achieved."
Some kami attacks during the war were rife with trickery, subterfuge, and subtlety, draining hope and pride from the mortal world. Other attacks were a lot more straightforward.
Man versus nature is not a fair fight.
"Just the thing for those pesky water mages." —Jaya Ballard, task mage
"The noble work of our order is to infuse all life on Esper with etherium. Our goal will be reached more rapidly if new life is . . . suppressed."
Dust-spiked winds eroded the stones, but the ground where they had stood still holds power.
"To make a prairie it takes a clover and one bee,/ One clover, and a bee,/ And revery." —Emily Dickinson
Its wings disturb more than air.
"A river of lava is just another river to cross."
"I have been brought to this place and I cannot leave. I may be free of the amber, but I am still in prison."
"Those who endure in the face of suffering, those whose faith shines long in evil days, they shall see salvation." —*Song of All*, canto 904
